question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 815 through 824 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY IS WORK NOBODY ASKED FOR, DONE TO A MEASURE NOBODY SET, AND THE WHOLE OF EVERY CHAPTER IS WHERE THE PERSON STOPS. There is no customer in any of the ten, nobody is told, nobody is refused, nothing is carried between people and nothing is passed. Every job in the ten is finished and every job stays finished. THE STOP IS ALWAYS A FACT ABOUT THE MATERIAL, THE TOOL, THE GROUND OR THE LIGHT AND NEVER A PRINCIPLE, AND NO CHARACTER IN ANY OF THE TEN MAY SAY A SENTENCE ABOUT HOW MUCH IS ENOUGH OR THAT IT COULD HAVE BEEN LEFT.
family_why_this_and_not_the_nearest: 805 to 814 was two people doing the two halves of one job and neither learning of the other, and the second person was never in the room. Here every job is one person's and complete, and the second person is in the room in five of the ten and does nothing whatever to the work. 795 to 804 was a person unable to do what she had watched. 765 to 774 was a better way kept and holed. 625 to 634 was a decision and a reason given. 745 to 754 was coming to an edge and being kept there. The engine in all of those is a person, a fault, an answer or a boundary. The engine here is judgement and what it costs the person to act on it, and there is nobody in the chapter to hand the judgement to.

anti_tick_rules_written_before_any_prose: THE FACT THAT NOBODY ASKED FOR ANY OF IT MAY BE STATED OUTRIGHT IN AT MOST FOUR OF THE TEN CHAPTERS. IN THE OTHER SIX IT CAN ONLY BE INFERRED. TEN CHAPTERS OF NOBODY ASKED FOR IT IS A TICK AND NOT A FAMILY.

THE STOP MAY NOT ARRIVE AT THE SAME PLACE IN THE PROSE. IN 0816, 0817, 0820 AND 0823 THE STOP IS DECIDED IN THE MIDDLE OF THE CHAPTER AND THE REST OF THE CHAPTER IS ABOUT LIVING WITH IT. IN 0815, 0818, 0819, 0821, 0822 AND 0824 IT IS THE LAST THING THAT HAPPENS.

NO CHAPTER MAY END ON THE WORK ITSELF BEING FINISHED. FOUR OF THE TEN END ON A PHYSICAL CHANGE THAT IS NOT THE WORK: 0818 THE CLIPPINGS, 0820 THE DAMP PATCH ON THE WALL, 0822 THE STREET, 0823 THE TWO EMPTY HOLES. THE OTHER SIX END ON SOMETHING THE WORK HAS REVEALED OR LEFT BEHIND.
NO CHARACTER MAY BE TOLD HOW MUCH ENOUGH IS AND NO CHARACTER MAY SAY IT. IF A LINE OF DIALOGUE COULD BE TRANSFERRED VERBATIM INTO ANY OTHER CHAPTER OF THE TEN IT IS OUT.
THE SECOND PERSON NEVER TOUCHES THE JOB. NO CARD MAY HAVE A SECOND PAIR OF HANDS IN IT, NOBODY HOLDS ANYTHING FOR THE PERSON WORKING, AND THE WORK IS COMPLETE WITHOUT THEM.

the_ten_stems: 0815 Friday the twenty-sixth of May 2023, in this borough. She is out in her own side passage at number twelve from the middle of the morning until the sun has come off the top of the boundary wall, and about nine feet of paving that has heaved at one end is the whole of that Friday.
0816 Wednesday the thirty-first of May 2023, in her own back yard at number ten for most of that Wednesday, and a strip of gravel path that has gone over with moss is the whole of it.

0817 Saturday the third of June 2023, along the boundary behind that lock-up from the time the shutter goes up to the time it comes down, and three lengths of paling that have been knocked out of line are the whole of that Saturday.

0818 Tuesday the sixth of June 2023, along the front of her own path at number nine from the time the sun clears the roof of the house opposite until it has gone off the flags, and twenty feet of grass that has come over the edge of it is the whole of that Tuesday.

0819 Saturday the tenth of June 2023, in his own office cabin at that unit for the whole of that Saturday, and a window frame that has dropped a quarter of an inch and knocks in any wind at all is the whole of it.

0820 Tuesday the thirteenth of June 2023, in her own yard at number ten from after the middle of the day until the light has gone off that wall, and six slabs standing on edge against it that have begun to slide are the whole of that Tuesday.

0821 Monday the nineteenth of June 2023, along his own boundary at that unit from the middle of the morning until the shadow of that shed has crossed the whole of it, and a length of privet that has gone woody at the bottom is the whole of that Monday.

0822 Thursday the twenty-second of June 2023, at the front of her own house at number nine, out on the kerb and in her garden from the middle of the morning until there is no light on the front of that house any more, and a limb off the plane tree that has lain across her fence since the winter is the whole of that Thursday.

0823 Sunday the twenty-fifth of June 2023, at the back of that lock-up from the middle of the morning until that bay has been in the dark a while, and a fence door hanging by one strap along that boundary is the whole of that Sunday.

0824 Friday the thirtieth of June 2023, in her own back garden at number twelve from the middle of the afternoon until the light has gone off the top of it, and a raised bed of broken brick that is leaning out of line at one end is the whole of that Friday.

cards.0815: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has about nine feet of a paving strip in her own side passage that has heaved at one end where the root of a lilac goes under it, and means to take the three flags up, level the ground that has been lifted and put them back; **she lifts the fourth flag as well, then stops, because a bar put down under the fourth goes through sound ground in one push and the ground beyond the fourth has not moved, and the whole chapter is the difference between a base that has moved and a base that has not.**
cards.0816: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a strip of gravel path about ten feet long in her own back yard that has gone over with moss and that she means to scarify back to stone; **she stops where the colour of the stone comes up under the moss and not an inch below it, and everything past that is not moss on top of gravel but moss in the making of a new surface, and the whole chapter is the colour.**
cards.0817: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has three lengths of bowed paling along the boundary at the back of that bay that have been knocked out of line and that she means to reset on new posts; **a bowed length is right at one end of a run and wrong at the other, and she sets all three at the top end because the eye takes the line of a fence from the far end of it, and a bow in the middle is the first thing anybody sees and a bow at the end is not, and the whole chapter is that decision and the eye that makes it.**
cards.0818: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has about twenty feet of grass along the front edge of her own path that has come over the kerb and out onto the flags and that she means to cut back; **there are two lines available, the line of the kerb and the line where the grass actually started before it came over, and they are about three inches apart and only one of them is the edge of anything, and she stops on the second one and the whole chapter is the three inches and the reason she can find it and the reason nobody else can.**
cards.0819: At the unit a man in his early forties has the window frame of his own office cabin that has dropped a quarter of an inch at the head and knocks on its stop in any wind at all; **he means to close the gap and finds that the gap is not the draught and never was, that the frame is heavy at the top corner and light at the bottom, and that the whole chapter is a strip of foam packed into a rebate and a knock that stops without the draught ever having been the point.**
cards.0820: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has six slabs standing on edge against a wall in her own yard that have begun to slide and go over; **she lays them flat on two battens out of the wet, and every one of them goes face up, and the reason is that a slab laid the wrong way up ponds on its own face, and the whole chapter is which way up a slab goes and how she can tell without a level.**
cards.0821: At the unit a man in his early forties has a run of privet along the boundary at the back of his own yard about six feet long that has gone over the fence and lost its bottom two feet to wood; **he cuts it back to where the leaf is and no lower, because privet cuts to a bare stem and a privet cut to a bare stem puts out two where there was one, and the whole chapter is the line of the cut and what is behind the privet that had not been seen since the spring.**
cards.0822: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a limb off the plane tree on the far side of the road that has lain across her front fence since the winter, half of it in the street and half of it in her garden, and that she means to cut up; **she cuts each length so that she can get it over that fence from the kerb without getting a hand under it to help, and the whole chapter is a length set by a fence and not by a limb.**
cards.0823: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a fence door at the back of that bay hanging by one strap where the screws have pulled out of the end grain; **she takes the leaf off its hinges, opens the strap, moves the fixings into sound timber as far as the strap allows and hangs it back, and the whole chapter is that the answer is not a longer screw and is not the same hole.**
cards.0824: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a raised bed of broken brick in her own back garden about nine feet long that has begun to lean out of line at the near end; **she takes the leaning end out and puts it back, and the sight down the length of that bed stops bending over one course at the near end where there was no good brick left and she used what was in the bucket, and the whole chapter is that one course and the sight-line over it.**

movement: Ten jobs, ten sound methods with no fault in any of them, ten jobs nobody asked for, and ten chapters about the moment each person stops. 0815 a paving strip lifted and the fourth flag put back down because the base under it has not moved. 0816 a mossy strip scarified to the colour of the stone and not an inch below. 0817 three bowed lengths set at the top of a run because that is where a bow stops showing. 0818 an edge cut to the line the grass started on and not to the line of the kerb. 0819 a strip of foam into a rebate and a knock that stops. 0820 six slabs laid face up on two battens. 0821 six feet of privet cut to the leaf and the fence behind it seen for the first time since the spring. 0822 a limb cut to a length set by a fence. 0823 a fence door hung back on two straps in sound timber with the old holes left empty. 0824 a bed of broken brick straight again except for one course and the sight that bends over it. Every job is dry work, every job is done from the ground, and no job in the ten needs a roof, a ladder, a loft or a manhole.
closing_images: TEN, AND NOT ONE OF THEM A THING PUT AWAY, AND NOT ONE OF THEM THE SHAPE OF ANOTHER. 0815 the cut face of the lilac root, pale and wet where the spade went through it, and going grey in a fortnight on its own. 0816 a stripe of the old colour showing through the new stone in the middle of that path, and the moss in a heap at the edge of it that will be a heap on that spot until it rots. 0817 the bow still in the run at the top end of it, where she put it on purpose, with the line of that fence going true from the gate to about three lengths and then not. 0818 the arisings going over the front of that path on the wind and a fine green film left along the top of the kerb, because a cut edge is not a finished edge until the grass is off it. 0819 the frame still a quarter of an inch low where it has been for two years, and the knock gone out of it entirely, which is a different thing from the draught and he knows that it is. 0820 the six slabs flat on their two battens and the damp patch on the wall behind them going pale at its edges. 0821 the fence behind the privet, which had not been seen since the spring the hedge went in, and the cut face of it on both sides of him. 0822 the street with nothing in it that came off it, and the last length of that limb going through the gap at the front of the house on its side. 0823 the door swinging on two straps and shutting, and the two old holes still in that timber, empty, above the line where the strap used to be. 0824 the sight down the length of that bed bending over one course at the near end.
